describes: House 107's working: how a classical timber house of the 1820s in Stavanger was clad, trimmed, roofed and set on its stones, and how 1986's boarding was nailed over its openings. The corner generator (corner.py) reads it with 107's record (fixtures/lt1-street.json) and the pack's materials; a missing key is an error. Millimetres unless named; a pair is a range the seed draws in.
provenance: Carried from the pack's classical working (packs/stavanger-1989/timber.json at 7fecfae, removed with the old house pipeline on 28 October) and docs/research/house-lessons.md (Measures); the bends and chamfers from docs/research/house-asset-craft.md (Recipe: house 107) and the finishing test's brief.

push.describes: The style's push on true sizes (the street's shape language: deep reveals, thick trims, sills and caps that throw a shadow): factors on the working's sizes.

chamferMm.describes: Each exposed arris worn round to about 2 px at the street stop (20 m): 15 to 20 mm on the big members, about 6 mm on small ones (house-asset-craft.md, Recipe 2).

bends.describes: Old timber moves, and every bend has a cause. The corner the house is seen from settles on its stones and the frame follows it down; the wall plate sags between the gables under the roof, most at the eave and none at the sill; the roof's thrust pushes the wall's head out. Each grows with the frame's age to a most; which corner settles is the seed's, claiming no history.
